planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in full sun to light shade and well-drained, lean soil; this selection tolerates a wider range of exposure and soil than the straight species.

directions: This selection of Lindheimer muhly was chosen for its brighter, honey-gold flower plumes that emerge in late summer and age to a glowing silvery tan through fall, giving a warmer color effect than the species' typical blue-silver haze. It forms the same large, stately clumps of fine blue-green foliage as straight Lindheimer muhly but tends to hold its upright form well without flopping, making it useful as a specimen or in mass plantings along Gulf Coast and Texas Hill Country landscapes. Unlike many muhly selections, this cultivar is noted for handling a broad range of light conditions, from reflected desert heat to fairly shaded sites, and adapts to most well-drained soil types. Cut clumps back hard in late winter before new growth resumes to keep the following season's plumes clean and full.
